explanation: The V32I substitution introduces an additional methyl group on the isoleucine side chain, increasing hydrophobic volume by ~27 Ų while maintaining the same charge and similar hydrophobicity. Since V32 directly contacts indinavir at a distance of 4.1 Å within the S2/S2' subpocket, this extra bulk creates a steric clash that destabilizes the van der Waals packing interface between the inhibitor and this critical binding pocket. The mutation essentially overcrowds a confined region of the binding site, forcing indinavir into a suboptimal conformation or reducing the favorable hydrophobic contacts that normally stabilize binding.
